title: Nashville
events_chronological: A sound truck for the presidential candidate Hal Phillip Walker circles the city broadcasting his platform to nobody in particular.
The country star Haven Hamilton records a bicentennial anthem while a reporter called Opal wanders the studio talking into a tape recorder.
Barbara Jean, the most loved singer in the city, collapses at her own airport welcome and is taken to hospital.
A pile-up on the freeway strands most of the city's musicians and hangers-on together for an entire afternoon.
Linnea Reese sings with a gospel choir while her husband Del negotiates with the candidate's organiser John Triplette.
The folk trio Tom, Bill and Mary record together while Tom sleeps with women from every other storyline.
Kenny Fraiser arrives in the city carrying a violin case and takes a room from an old man whose wife is dying in hospital.
Winifred, a waitress who has walked out on her husband, keeps trying to get onto any stage that will let her sing.
Sueleen Gay, who cannot sing at all, performs at a men's smoker and is made to strip for the room.
Barbara Jean is let out of hospital and breaks down on stage, rambling to the audience until she is led off.
Haven Hamilton refuses to appear at the candidate's rally unless his own conditions are met.
Linnea sleeps with Tom after his set and goes home afterwards to her deaf children.
The old man's wife dies in hospital, and his lodger does not notice.
Triplette assembles the rally by promising every performer a different thing.
Barbara Jean sings at the rally and is shot in front of the crowd by the young man with the violin case.
Haven Hamilton, hit in the arm, tells the crowd that this is their city and hands the microphone to Winifred.
Winifred takes the stage at last and leads the crowd in a song while the ambulances pull away.
The crowd keeps singing as the camera withdraws over their heads.
syuzhet_notes: The film cuts constantly between two dozen people over five days, usually on a song or a passing car, so consecutive told-order bullets belong to different lives rather than to different times. Nothing is a flashback.
fabula_notes: The five days are continuous and the ordering follows from who is where. Strands that overlap in time can be ranked either way without changing anything.
